name: run
title: Run a shell command
description: Run one command line with Inferno sh inside the session sandbox and wait for it to finish. Inferno sh is NOT bash: quote with single quotes only ('it''s' doubles the quote), group with { }, lists are (a b c), the exit status is a string in $status (empty means success), and if/for/while exist only after `load std` (`load std; if {test -f x} {echo yes} {echo no}`). There is no $(...), no double-quote quoting, no && inside [ ], no 2>&1 (write >[2=1]). Substitute a command with `{cmd}. The server instructions hold a longer primer. Changes to the namespace (bind, mount) persist for later calls; environment variables and the working directory do not, because sh copies its environment. Programs still running when the command line ends keep running until `reset` or the end of the session, but lose their output; start such programs with job_start instead. Returns stdout and stderr as text (bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD; use read_file for binary data), the exit status string, and flags telling whether the command timed out and was killed or its output was cut at the cap.

command.description: The sh command line. It may hold several commands and newlines.

stdin.description: Text given to the command on standard input. Without it, standard input is empty.

cwd.description: Directory to run in, for this call only. Default /tmp.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the command and everything it started after this many milliseconds. Default 30000.

max_output_bytes.description: Keep at most this many bytes of stdout and of stderr; the rest is dropped and the truncated flag set. Default 65536.

stdout.description: Standard output, up to the cap.

stderr.description: Standard error (diagnostics), up to the cap.

status.description: Inferno exit status: empty for success, otherwise text such as fail:errors or killed.

ok.description: True if the status is empty and the command did not time out.

timed_out.description: True if the timeout expired and the command was killed.

stdout_truncated.description: True if stdout was longer than the cap.

stderr_truncated.description: True if stderr was longer than the cap.

note.description: Present only when the program ran into a limit of the session: its memory (all its programs together) or the number of programs it may run, or, for a job, its timeout_ms. Says which.

name: read_file
title: Read a file
description: Read bytes from a file, starting at `offset`. The content comes back as text when the bytes are valid UTF-8 and as base64 otherwise; `encoding` says which. A read that would end inside a multi-byte character stops before it. To read a large file, call again with offset set to the previous offset plus `bytes`, until `eof` is true.

path.description: File name in the session's namespace. Absolute (/tmp/x), or relative to /tmp.

offset.description: Byte offset to start at. Default 0.

encoding.description: auto (default): text if valid UTF-8, else base64. base64: always base64.

content.description: The bytes read, as text or base64.

bytes.description: Number of bytes read (before any base64 encoding).

size.description: Length of the file in bytes, as stat reports it.

eof.description: True if the read reached the end of the file.

name: write_file
title: Write a file
description: Write `content` to a file. mode truncate (default) replaces the file or creates it; create makes a new file and fails with `file already exists` if there is one; append adds to the end, creating the file if needed. The directory must exist (make it with run: mkdir -p dir). Use encoding base64 for bytes that are not UTF-8 text.

path.description: File name in the session's namespace. Absolute (/tmp/x), or relative to /tmp.

content.description: What to write: text, or base64 when encoding is base64.

encoding.description: How content is encoded. Default utf8.

name: list_dir
title: List a directory
description: List the entries of a directory, sorted by name, with type, size, permission bits and modification time. A union directory lists every member, so a name can appear twice.

path.description: File name in the session's namespace. Absolute (/tmp/x), or relative to /tmp.

name.description: Last element of the file name.

mode.description: Permission bits in octal, e.g. 644. Owner, group, other.

append_only.description: True if writes always go to the end (Inferno DMAPPEND).

truncated.description: True if the directory has more entries than were returned.

name: stat
title: Describe a file
description: Return the Inferno directory entry of a file or directory: type, size, permission bits, times, owner and group. Fails with `file does not exist` when there is no such file, which makes it the way to test for one.

path.description: File name in the session's namespace. Absolute (/tmp/x), or relative to /tmp.

name.description: Last element of the file name.

mode.description: Permission bits in octal, e.g. 644. Owner, group, other.

append_only.description: True if writes always go to the end (Inferno DMAPPEND).

muid.description: User who last modified the file.

name: remove
title: Remove a file or directory
description: Remove a file or an empty directory. With recursive true, remove a directory and everything in it. Files outside the writable parts of the sandbox (such as /bin and /lib) fail with `file system read only`.

path.description: File name in the session's namespace. Absolute (/tmp/x), or relative to /tmp.

recursive.description: Also remove the contents of a directory. Default false.

removed.description: Number of files and directories removed.

name: job_start
title: Start a background job
description: Start a long-running or interactive program and return at once with its job id. Give `command`, an sh command line (the same Inferno sh as run), or `argv`, a program and its arguments run without sh. The job runs in the session's namespace with pipes for its standard input, output and error. Read its output with job_read, feed its input with job_write, stop it with job_kill. Jobs end with reset and with the session.

command.description: An sh command line. Give this or argv.

argv.description: A program and its arguments, such as ["cat", "-"]. The program is found as sh finds it (cat is /bin/cat.wasm). Give this or command.

stdin.description: Text written to the job's standard input first. More can follow with job_write.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the job and everything it started after this many milliseconds. Default: no limit; it runs until job_kill, reset or the end of the session.

id.description: The job id, for the other job tools.

pid.description: The job's prog id, as ps and /prog show it.

name: job_read
title: Read a job's output
description: Return a job's output from an offset, and whether it has exited. Offsets count bytes from the start of each stream; by default a read starts where the last one ended, so calling job_read repeatedly returns new output only. With wait_ms, wait up to that long for output or for the job to exit; other calls are answered meanwhile. The server keeps the last 1 MiB of each stream: older output is dropped and counted in `lost`, and the job is never stopped by output nobody reads.

offset.description: Where to start in standard output. Default: where the last job_read ended.

stderr_offset.description: Where to start in standard error. Default: where the last job_read ended.

wait_ms.description: If there is no new output, wait up to this many milliseconds for some, or for the exit. Default 0.

max_bytes.description: Most bytes of each stream to return. Default 65536.

stdout.description: Standard output from `offset`. Bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD.

offset.description: Offset of the first byte of stdout returned.

next_offset.description: Offset after the last byte of stdout returned.

stderr_offset.description: Offset of the first byte of stderr returned.

next_stderr_offset.description: Offset after the last byte of stderr returned.

lost.description: Bytes of stdout before `offset` that were asked for but already dropped.

running.description: True until the job has exited and its output is all collected.

status.description: Inferno exit status once it has exited: empty for success, otherwise text such as fail:errors or killed.

ok.description: True if the job has exited with an empty status.

note.description: Present only when the program ran into a limit of the session: its memory (all its programs together) or the number of programs it may run, or, for a job, its timeout_ms. Says which.

name: job_write
title: Write to a job's input
description: Queue `data` for a job's standard input and return at once; the bytes reach the job as it reads them, in order. With eof true, close the input after the data, so the job reads end of file.

data.description: What to write: text, or base64 when encoding is base64. Default empty.

encoding.description: How data is encoded. Default utf8.

eof.description: Close the job's input after this data. Default false.
True if the input is closed or will be once the queue is written.

name: job_kill
title: Stop a job
description: Kill a job and every program it started. job_read then reports the exit, with status killed. A job that has already exited is left as it is.

killed.description: True if the job was running and has been sent the kill.

name: job_list
title: List jobs
description: List the session's jobs, running and exited, with their ids, commands and exit status. Exited jobs are kept until there are more than 32 of them.

command.description: The command line, or the argv joined with spaces.

running.description: True until the job has exited.

name: ns
title: Show the namespace
description: Return the session's namespace as Inferno's ns command prints it: one bind or mount command per line, in the order that rebuilds it.

ns.description: The namespace, as ns prints it.

name: bind
title: Bind a file or directory
description: Make `to` refer to `from` in the session's namespace, as Inferno's bind does. order replace (default) hides what was at `to`; before and after make a union directory with `from` searched first or last. create lets new files be made in `from` through the union. Devices (#U, #C, #I ...) cannot be named: the session has given up the right to attach them, and binding one fails with `mount/attach disallowed`. Lasts until reset.

create.description: Allow creation in from through to. Default false.

name: mount
title: Mount a file server
description: Mount a 9P (Styx) file server on `to` in the session's namespace, as Inferno's mount command does. `source` is a dial string (tcp!host!port, which needs /net granted to the session) or a {command} block run by sh with a pipe as its standard input and output, such as {memfs -s}. The mount authenticates when the server asks, unless authenticate is false. Lasts until reset.

source.description: A dial string or a {command} block.

create.description: Allow creation through the mount point. Default false.

authenticate.description: Authenticate if the server asks. Default true.

timeout_ms.description: Give up after this many milliseconds. Default 30000.

name: unmount
title: Undo a bind or mount
description: Remove `from` from the union at `to`, or with no `from`, everything bound or mounted at `to`, as Inferno's unmount does.

from.description: The member to remove. Default: all of them.

name: reset
title: Start a fresh session
description: Kill every program the session started and rebuild its namespace: /tmp is empty again, and binds, mounts and environment variables made by earlier calls are gone. Use it to recover from a broken namespace or to start a task from a clean state.

reset.description: Always true: the session is new.
